pageCache.pageTitle: Home - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Home
Welcome
Welcomefrom the Headteacher
I am proud to be the Headteacher of this wonderful school. Kington St Michael is a caring, close-knit community where children, staff and families work together to ensure every child thrives.
Our school offers a welcoming and nurturing environment where children have the space to learn, play and grow. Our vision, ‘Learning together, aiming high’, reflects our belief that by working together, every child can achieve their full potential.
We would be delighted to welcome you to visit and see our wonderful school in action.
Foundations for SuccessThe KSM Difference
Wonderful Community
At Kington St Michael, we pride ourselves on being a warm, welcoming and inclusive community. Our school thrives because of the strong partnerships between staff, governors, parents, carers and pupils, all working together to provide the best possible experiences for every child.
Our governors play a key role in supporting the school, helping to shape its vision and ensuring high standards are maintained. The Friends of KSM School Committee, run by an enthusiastic group of parents, enhances our children’s education by providing activities, equipment and resources beyond what the school budget can cover.
Family and community involvement is at the heart of school life. Parents and carers regularly support reading with children, helping on trips, and volunteering in classrooms, creating rich learning experiences. Pupils enjoy a wide range of community celebrations and events, including sports day, nativity performances, concerts and end-of-year productions, all of which bring the school together and showcase pupils’ talents.
Charity work is also central to our ethos. Through fundraising for causes such as Bristol Children’s Hospital, Chippenham Doorway Foodbank and Children in Need, children develop a strong sense of empathy, kindness and social responsibility.
This supportive, collaborative community ensures that every child feels valued, connected and inspired; creating a school where children, families and staff flourish together.
Academic Success
Our teaching is of the highest calibre. Every member of staff is an experienced, well-qualified professional, deeply committed to each child’s progress. This year, we achieved a 100% success rate in the Phonics and Early Reading Assessment (PERA), reflecting how solidly we build confidence and foundational skills in our youngest learners. Pupils perform exceptionally well in statutory assessments, consistently exceeding both local and national outcomes.
We embrace technology to make learning engaging and inspiring, using a variety of IT equipment to bring lessons to life. Alongside this, we place great value on traditional skills – teaching children to handwrite beautifully, nurturing a love of books and reading, and planning rich, creative lessons across all subjects.
Ofsted’s most recent inspection (February 2025) captured our ethos perfectly, noting: 'This is a nurturing and happy school, where pupils enjoy learning. The school has high aspirations for what pupils can achieve. Pupils meet these expectations. They work hard and achieve well across the curriculum.'
Outdoor Learning
Set in the beautiful Wiltshire countryside, our school provides a welcoming and nurturing environment where children have the space to learn, play and grow. Our extensive outdoor areas include an Early Years garden, a mud kitchen, and a brand-new Forest School space, offering pupils endless opportunities to explore, discover and be active.
Playtimes are lively and varied, with skipping ropes, ball games, rounders, hopscotch, giant chess and more. For children seeking a quieter moment, benches and picnic tables create inviting spots for reading and conversation. We also offer a lunchtime Dove Club, run by our pastoral lead. Our buddy system pairs older and younger pupils, fostering strong friendships, kindness and a true sense of community.
Surrounded by fruit trees, a vegetable patch and our flourishing school garden, children develop a deep appreciation for nature and the environment – learning first hand the value of care, curiosity and outdoor adventure in a safe, supportive setting.
Wraparound Care
Our school offers a welcoming breakfast and after-school club, known as ‘The Nest’, providing high-quality wraparound care for children of parents and carers who require additional support outside of school hours. The Nest runs every weekday in the school hall from 7:40am to 6:00pm, led by a wonderful, experienced team committed to making every session enjoyable and enriching.
The emphasis at The Nest is on play and leisure, with opportunities for children to complete reading or homework if they wish. A wide range of activities and games are available, including puzzles, board games, air hockey, pool, drawing and colouring, themed craft projects, model making, LEGO, small-world play, and a variety of outdoor games and sports to promote physical development.
Personal Development
We are proud that Ofsted graded our personal development provision 'Outstanding', noting:
'The personal development offer for pupils is impressive. Pupils learn about fundamental British values exceptionally well, talking with maturity about the importance of individual liberty and mutual respect. They understand why discrimination is wrong… Pupils are very well prepared for life beyond school.'
At Kington St Michael, we focus on developing children’s character alongside their academic success. Pupils enjoy a wide range of clubs and enrichment activities, trips and sports, and leadership opportunities such as school and worship councils, play buddy schemes, and leading assemblies.
Through our values programme, collective worship and real-life experiences, pupils grow in confidence, resilience and kindness – preparing them exceptionally well for life beyond school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our SchoolHeadteacher's Welcome
Welcome Message
My name is Mrs Victoria O’Brien and I am proud to be the Headteacher of this wonderful school. Kington St Michael is a caring, close-knit community where children, staff and families work together to ensure every child thrives.
Set in the beautiful Wiltshire countryside, our school offers a welcoming and nurturing environment where children have the space to learn, play and grow. With large outdoor areas, an early years garden, a mud kitchen and a developing forest school, pupils enjoy plenty of opportunities to explore, be active and appreciate nature. Our buddy system helps build strong friendships across year groups, fostering kindness and community.
Our vision, ‘Learning together, aiming high’, reflects our belief that by working together, every child can achieve their full potential. Our dedicated staff provide a rich, creative curriculum that inspires curiosity, confidence and a love of learning.
We are proud of our reputation as a happy and high-achieving school. Ofsted (February 2025) described us as 'a nurturing and happy school, where pupils enjoy learning…a welcoming place where everyone is nice to one another.' We couldn’t agree more!
This is a place where children feel known, valued and inspired – and where learning is exciting, purposeful and fun. We would be delighted to welcome you to visit and see our wonderful school in action.
Mrs Victoria O’BrienHeadteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: British Values - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Key InformationBritish Values
Text
At KSM, we actively embrace the British Values of mutual respect, tolerance, the rule of law, democracy, and individual liberty. These principles are shared by many cultures and countries across the world, and they help prepare our pupils to become responsible, respectful and active members of society. Alongside these, we also foster a wider set of values that underpin our school community. All of these values are woven throughout our curriculum, and we are proud of the many ways we teach, model and celebrate them.
Through everyday school life, assemblies and classroom learning, we nurture qualities such as generosity, compassion, courage, forgiveness, friendship, and respect. Each term, we focus on a specific value in greater depth, exploring its meaning and importance through stories, discussion, activities and reflection. This approach helps our pupils to develop a strong moral foundation and to grow into thoughtful, caring and responsible individuals.
In addition, we ensure pupils understand how British Values apply to real-life situations. They learn about democracy through opportunities such as school council elections and class decision-making. They explore the rule of law by discussing fairness, understanding school rules, and learning about how laws keep us safe. Individual liberty is encouraged by helping children make informed choices in a secure environment, while respect and tolerance are taught through learning about different cultures, beliefs and perspectives, both within our school and in the wider community.
Together, these experiences help our children develop the knowledge, skills and attitudes they need to thrive as respectful and active members of modern Britain.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Key InformationCollective Worship
Text
Collective worship is an important part of the school day at Kington St Michael CE Primary School. It is a special time where we come together to worship and reflect on our school vision and values. We want to make the most of our opportunities in Collective Worship; developing our children’s spirituality and their understanding, awareness and appreciation of those messages and beliefs founded through our faith and the value we have for all around us.
At KSM our Collective Worship aims to be inclusive, invitational and inspiring.
Through Collective Worship, we aim to give the children opportunities:
To recognise the place Christian faith has in the lives of people.
Develop a sense of wonder, awe, curiosity and mystery.
Understand the difference between right and wrong and the consequences of their actions for themselves and for others.
Be creative, questioning and imaginative within a broad Christian framework that recognises the importance of experience, personal values and respect for the beliefs of others.
Recognise, respect and celebrate cultural diversity.
See the relevance of Christian tradition in their own lives.
To be part of the planning process for Collective Worship so it is meaningful to them.
Pupil participation and pupil voice is an important part of our collective worship. Our KS2 Worship Council make a significant contribution to our Collective Worship and Church festivals. Our School Worship Team write a prayer to begin Governor Meetings.

pageCache.pageTitle: Christian Vision and Values - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our SchoolChristian Vision and Values
Text
KSM Christian Vision
Our vision was born out of our Christian foundation and reflects the needs of our school community and local context.
Within our Christian community, our village school nurtures growth and creates opportunities for everyone’s unique strengths to blossom.
We provide the rich soil that enables our children to develop deep roots, grow and flourish.
Our vision underpins all that we do at KSM. All members of our KSM family are equally valued, respect themselves and others, and have high hopes for the brightest of futures.
KSM Biblical Root
Our Christian vision is underpinned by the Bible verse Colossians 2.7 (Good News Bible).
Keep your roots deep in him,
Build your lives on him,
And become stronger in your faith.
KSM School Christian Values
At KSM our vision is underpinned by our 6 clear core values, which drive the way we behave and interact with one another. Our values are woven throughout our entire school life to create a learning community built on love and joy, in which we nurture, grow and flourish.
Trust: 'My God is my strength in whom I trust' (Psalm 18.2) helps us to learn about being trustworthy and being there for our friends when they need us.
Friendship: ‘A friend is always loyal and a brother is born to help in time of need’ (Proverbs 17:17). A true friend is always loving, loyal and helps in trying times.
Courage: ‘Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid’. (Deuteronomy 31.6) Children are encouraged to embrace courage and strength because God is always with them.
Respect: 'Do to others as you would have them do to you' (Matthew 7.12) helps us all to value other people, places and opinions that may be different to our own.
Forgiveness: ‘Be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other just as Christ God forgave you’. (Ephesians 4:32) Respond to others with kindness and forgiveness.
Hope: ‘May the God of hope fill you with joy and peace’ (Romans 15:13) Put your trust in God to have joy and peace, which leads to overflowing hope!
At KSM our vision and values are at the core of everything we do. We support, encourage and nurture everyone to aspire to be the best possible versions of themselves so that they realise their full potential – both in their learning and in their relationships.
Nurture Grow Flourish

pageCache.pageTitle: A Church School - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our SchoolA Church School
Text
As a church school, our Christian faith is at the heart of our school life. Our Headteacher and staff work together to nurture and celebrate the school’s distinctive Christian character through everyday school life and the curriculum.
We gather each day for meaningful Christian worship and offer a school experience rooted in Christian values such as love, kindness, forgiveness and respect. Religious education and learning about worldviews are valued parts of our curriculum, helping children to understand and respect others.
We are proud to be part of the Bristol Diocese and enjoy a strong and supportive relationship. Throughout the year, we celebrate the major Christian festivals together, while also recognising and celebrating other festivals, helping our children grow in understanding, joy and respect for the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parent Helpers and Volunteers - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
ParentsParent Helpers and Volunteers
Text
We warmly welcome parents who would like to offer their time and skills to support our KSM school community. Volunteering can make a real difference to children’s learning and experiences, and there are many ways you can get involved:
Hearing individual readers
Supporting on swimming days
Helping in the library
Accompanying school trips
Running specialist sessions based on your skills, e.g., science, history, art, French
Cooking with children
Volunteering can be on a regular basis, such as weekly, or for specific sessions. All volunteers receive guidance and training from the Teaching and Safeguarding Team.
We are extremely fortunate to have a dedicated group of parents and volunteers, helping to support children’s learning across the school.
If you are interested in volunteering, please speak to Mrs. Allott or Miss Gardner, in the school office. We are always keen to hear from new volunteers and welcome fresh ideas and experiences to share with our children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningMusic
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
The Intent of our music curriculum is to foster a lifelong love of music, develop musical skills (singing, playing, composing and listening), build confidence and creativity and encourage an appreciation for diverse cultures through all types of music.
Through regular exposure to diverse and exciting artists and musicians, children will be encouraged to listen, question, compose, compare and improve what they hear. Through high quality performances and recordings, children will be engaged and inspired to develop a love of music and improve their musical talents in order increase their own self-confidence, creativity and sense of achievement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clubs - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
ParentsClubs
Text
After-School Clubs
We offer a wide range of after-school activities to cater to as many interests as possible. Clubs are run by staff and specialist teachers or coaches, and are available to all children. Staff-led sessions run from the end of school until 4:15pm; sports clubs run until 4:25pm.
Some of the clubs we have on offer include:
Craft, Football, Gardening, Crochet, Mindfulness, Film, LEGO, STEM, Mathematics, Art, French, German, and Forest School.
Specialist Coaching
Our specialist coaching provider is Up and Under Sports.
Applying for Clubs
All parents and carers are invited to apply for clubs prior to each term. The clubs on offer may change each term to ensure a wide variety of options.
Make sure to apply for the appropriate club for your child’s class or year group.
If a club is oversubscribed, places will be allocated according to a waiting list.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care – The Nest - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
ParentsWraparound Care – The Nest
Text
The Nest runs Monday to Thursday from 7:40am to 6pm and Friday 7:40am to 5pm, led by a wonderful team committed to making every session enjoyable and enriching. The emphasis at The Nest is on play and leisure, with opportunities for children to complete reading or homework if they wish. A wide range of activities and games is available, including puzzles, board games, air hockey, pool, drawing and colouring, themed craft projects, model making, LEGO, small-world play, and a variety of outdoor games and sports to promote physical development.
The Nest sessions are structured as follows:
7:40am–8:40am – £4.50 per session (includes breakfast)
8:15am–8:40am – £3.00 per session (does not include breakfast)
Monday - Friday - 3:25pm–5:00pm – £9.00 per session (includes a welcome snack and drink)
Monday - Thursday - 3:25pm–6:00pm – £14.00 per session (includes a welcome snack, drink and light tea served between 5:00pm-5:15pm)
Booking and payment are made through SCOPAY, and childcare vouchers are also accepted (please contact the school office to set this up). Places should be booked by midnight the night before attending, but short-notice bookings can be arranged by contacting the school office directly.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningArt and Design
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
Our Art and Design curriculum aims to inspire creativity, develop artistic skills and foster self-expression in every child. We believe that art is a vital part of a broad and balanced education, and provides all pupils with the opportunity to explore, communicate and reflect through visual and tactile experiences.
Our intent is to develop creativity and imagination by giving pupils the freedom to explore their ideas and express themselves through a range of artistic media and techniques. We aim to build technical skills progressively in drawing, painting, sculpture, and other craft and design techniques, enabling pupils to refine their work and build confidence in their abilities. We want to encourage critical thinking and reflection, allowing children to evaluate their own work and that of others using appropriate artistic vocabulary.
Our curriculum exposes pupils to a wide range of artists, designers and craft makers from different times, cultures and backgrounds, to broaden their understanding of the world and inspire their own artistic journey. In addition, we aim to promote resilience and experimentation, encouraging children to take creative risks, learn from mistakes and find enjoyment in the process of making art.
Finally, we aim to ensure inclusion and accessibility, enabling all pupils – including those with SEND and disadvantaged backgrounds – to engage fully and achieve success in art. Through high-quality art education, we aim to nurture confident, curious, and reflective young artists who appreciate the role of art in their own lives, in culture, and in the wider world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningComputing
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
Our intent in Primary Computing at Kington St. Michael is to inspire children to be confident, creative, and safe users of technology. Our curriculum prepares children to use technology confidently and responsibly, giving them skills that will support future learning and opportunities.
Children are encouraged to develop logical thinking and problem-solving skills through coding and computational tasks, for example, using Micro:bits, to bring their ideas to life. We want pupils to see themselves as digital creators who can design, innovate and collaborate effectively.
Our teaching promotes resilience and responsibility, with online safety and the role of our student Digital Leaders at the heart of the curriculum. Above all, our goal is to nurture curiosity and confidence so all pupils leave primary school ready to flourish in an ever-changing digital world.

pageCache.pageTitle: English - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningEnglish
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
Our English curriculum is designed to equip pupils with the language skills they need to become confident, effective communicators and lifelong readers and writers. We believe that a strong foundation in English is essential for success across the curriculum and beyond. Our primary intent is to build strong oracy skills to enable pupils to express themselves clearly, ask questions, debate, perform and engage respectfully in discussion.
Fostering a lifelong love of reading is a key aim of our curriculum. Exposing pupils to high quality texts from a diverse range of cultures and backgrounds supports our ethos of reading for pleasure. To establish this, early reading and phonics are the back bone of our English curriculum, ensuring pupils become fluent, confident readers through our systematic high quality phonics teaching.
Alongside our teaching of reading, we also ensure a consistent approach to teaching writing. A strong focus on transcription skills enables pupils to develop automaticity in their handwriting and spelling, freeing up their working memory to develop strong composition skills. This will, in turn, develop confident and creative writers who can write with purpose and accuracy using rich vocabulary and language.

pageCache.pageTitle: Geography - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningGeography
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
Our intent in our primary geography curriculum is to provide a broad and balanced geographical education that inspires an active curiosity about the world. It focuses on developing and extending children’s locational knowledge and geographical skills, whilst encouraging them to think critically and become independent learners. This links in with both literacy and numeracy skills when exploring, interpreting and presenting statistics.

pageCache.pageTitle: History - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningHistory
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
The intent of our primary History curriculum is to inspire curiosity about the past and help children understand how history has shaped the world they live in today. We aim to develop pupils’ knowledge of key events, people and societies, both locally and globally.
Through engaging and chronological learning, students will gain a strong sense of time, cause and effect, and change over time. Our curriculum encourages critical thinking, questioning, and the use of historical evidence. We want children to appreciate diversity, understand different perspectives, and make connections across periods and cultures. Ultimately, we aim to equip pupils with the skills to become thoughtful, informed, and active citizens.

pageCache.pageTitle: Maths - Kington St Michael CE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our LearningMaths
Statement of Intent
Statement of Intent
At our school, we believe that mathematics is essential to everyday life, critical to science, technology, and engineering, and necessary for financial literacy and most forms of employment. Our intent is to provide a high-quality mathematics education that inspires curiosity, develops deep conceptual understanding, and fosters a sense of enjoyment and confidence in maths.
We aim to ensure that all children:
Become fluent in the fundamentals of mathematics through varied and frequent practice, so they develop conceptual understanding and the ability to recall and apply knowledge with automaticity.
Reason mathematically by following a line of enquiry, identifying relationships and patterns, and using mathematical language to justify and explain their thinking.
Solve problems by applying their mathematics to a variety of increasingly complex problems, breaking them down into manageable steps and persevering in seeking solutions.
We provide a curriculum that is carefully sequenced, coherent, and cumulative, allowing children to build on prior knowledge and make connections across mathematical ideas. We use concrete, pictorial, and abstract approaches (CPA) to support all learners, and promote a mastery approach so that every child develops a secure and deep understanding of each mathematical concept.
We are committed to ensuring that our maths curriculum is inclusive and accessible, allowing all children – regardless of background or ability – to develop confidence, resilience, and a positive attitude towards maths that will support them throughout their education and beyond.

Statement of Intent
At Kington St Michael, our MFL teaching aims to spark curiosity and broaden pupils’ understanding of the world. We want children to develop the confidence to communicate in another language while enjoying their learning.
Lessons are designed to be fun, inclusive, and accessible to all. Alongside language skills, we encourage pupils to explore their own cultural identity and appreciate the cultures of others.
